newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Feb retail sales plunge 30.1 pct mth/mth.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Feb retail sales plunge 30.1 pct mth/mth.

text.p: Singapore's February retail sales index plunged 30.1 percent from January, dragged down by a drastic drop in car sales, and was down 17.6 percent from February 1996, the Statistics Department said.
It said motor vehicle sales in February fell 65.2 percent month-on-month and 61.1 percent year-on-year.
If motor vehicles were excluded, the index would have been down just 3.3 percent on a year-on-year basis, though the month-on-month fall would still have been steep at 19.4 percent.
The Statistics Department blamed the fall partly on seasonal factors, specifically a fall in spending after the flurry of festive buying for the important Chinese Lunar New Year holidays.
The Lunar New Year holidays were in early February this year. In 1996 they were in the latter half of the month.
Total February retail sales were estimated at Singapore $1.76 billion (US$1.22 billion).
The Statistics Department said that department store and supermarket sales were off 13.4 percent year-on-year in February, and 17.3 percent month-on-month.
That retail sector has been under pressure for some time, with several major department stores closing or trimming back in 1996.

The cutbacks came as Singapore's economic growth was generally slowing. The city-state's overall growth for 1996 was seven percent, significantly below the 8.8 percent expansion of 1995 and the double-digit gains in each of the previous two years.
This year the government has forecast growth within a five to seven percent range, hurt by a slowdown in electronics exports that began last year and has thus far continued in 1997.
